_metadata.description: 90% predictive ranges for direct jobs from the gambling coefficient, by land-based casino property type.
_metadata.method: Each state's direct jobs coefficient (jobs per $1M output) is compared with 2022 Economic Census employees per $1M receipts (2023 dollars) for the same state and property type, cells with at least 50 employees. No bias is detectable (geometric-mean ratios 0.94, 1.06, 0.96; p > 0.5), so the point estimate stays at the coefficient. p05/p95 are the 5th and 95th percentiles of a lognormal fitted to 1/(model/observed) across states, applied to direct jobs.
_metadata.why_not_calibrated: A QCEW test of jobs per WAGE dollar shows a shortfall, but the Census test, which observes revenue, attributes it to an overstated compensation share of revenue (which falls with the state gaming tax), not to too few jobs.
_metadata.scope: Direct jobs only; supplier and induced jobs have no observed benchmark. Not provided for bars with slots (no gaming-tavern benchmark), tribal properties (the Economic Census excludes most tribal casinos), online operations, or user-entered jobs.
_metadata.source: Philander, 'Multipliers for sectors that are not casinos' (in preparation); replication repository kphilander/casino-io-validation (script 19, analysis_output/output_side_jobs_ranges.csv; private until publication). Data: U.S. Census Bureau, 2022 Economic Census, EC2271BASIC and EC2272BASIC.
